module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mathoverflow 347178

*Reference:* [mathoverflow/347178](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/347178)
asked by user [*Biagio Ricceri*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/149235/biagio-ricceri)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Real Set
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Mathoverflow347178

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Is it true that
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x) = \sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$$?

Answer: No. A counterexample in $\mathbb R^2$ is recorded in the linked formal proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 26,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/fc20c0b55eab6fc26e2bb5b24fb3005303a0910b/FormalConjectures/Mathoverflow/347178.lean#L670"]
theorem mathoverflow_347178 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 f),
        (BddAbove (range f) ↔ BddAbove (range (fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)))) ∧
        (⨆ x, (f x : EReal)) = ⨆ x, (f (x + gradient f x) : EReal) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Is the boundedness of
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x)$ and $\sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$ equivalent?

Answer: No. The same counterexample is recorded in the linked formal proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 26,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/fc20c0b55eab6fc26e2bb5b24fb3005303a0910b/FormalConjectures/Mathoverflow/347178.lean#L690"]
theorem mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_iff :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 f),
        BddAbove (range f) ↔ BddAbove (range fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Does the equality
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x) = \sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$$
hold when both suprema are finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 26]
theorem mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_only :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
        (h : BddAbove (range f)) (h' : BddAbove (range (fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)))),
        (⨆ x, f x) = ⨆ x, f (x + gradient f x) := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow347178

reformulations.difference: The source asks only whether the two suprema are equal. Lean uses extended-real suprema and additionally conjoins equivalence of boundedness above.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The additional conjunct follows from the supremum equality: any real upper bound for one range bounds its extended-real supremum, hence also the equal supremum and every value of the other function. This works in both directions. Thus the conjunction is equivalent to the source’s equality, including unbounded cases. The full universally quantified RHS equivalence was proved as Review347178.main_rhs_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source answer discusses the variant assuming sup f is finite. Lean separately assumes boundedness above of both ranges and expresses the equality using real rather than extended-real suprema.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The range of x ↦ f(x + gradient f x) is contained in range f, so the second boundedness hypothesis follows from the first. Both ranges are nonempty because Euclidean space contains zero. Their real suprema therefore are genuine least upper bounds, and coercion to EReal preserves them. The full equivalence with the singly bounded, extended-real formulation was proved as Review347178.bounded_rhs_source_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: All three declarations faithfully state the question or its variants. The source’s two-dimensional counterexample has sup f = +∞ and sup f(x + ∇f(x)) = 0, agreeing with both fixed negative answers and solved tags. Its discussion leaves the general bounded-above variant unsettled, consistent with the open tag. Lean checks confirmed the quantifier scopes, genuine gradients under ContDiff ℝ 1, nonempty ranges, and constant-function boundary cases. Both equivalence proofs compiled without sorryAx. The linked formal_proof certificates were not opened because the task prohibits consulting formal-conjectures on GitHub; the source corroborates the recorded negative answers, but the certificates themselves were not audited.
